1.why: Two options fuse the finding with a second note (B finding+limitation, D finding+prior research); I take the limitation-bearing one, but this is a coin flip between B and D.

2.why: A, B and D are three bare dated innovations; C is the only option that states the trend they jointly form and carries the terminal date.

3.why: The only option joining two causes to two effects with an explicit 'Because'; A, B, C are single definitional notes.

4.why: C packs the most distinct notes (year, institution, N, duration, purpose) while A, B, D are one-fact findings, but no option integrates the findings so the axis is unclear.

5.why: Only B sets two notes against each other (self-rated alertness vs measured reaction time); A, C, D are single readings.

6.why: 'Taken together, the two experiments confirmed...' is the only option spanning both experiments and stating what they jointly show.

7.why: D is the only option joining two notes under one relation ('Two caveats temper the finding'), but B's emphatic restatement is an equally plausible key shape.

8.why: A carries the most notes under a causal 'because' (depth, cost, risk, equipment); C is a close rival that fuses method with finding.

9.why: Only C holds both distances in one contrastive frame; A and B are the halves and D drops the numbers entirely.

10.why: B alone binds all three scope notes (N, age band, duration) to a stated consequence; A lists them flat and C, D carry other notes.

11.why: D is the only generalization across the studies; A, B, C are single study details, one of them a counterexample.

12.why: C joins two limitation notes to a consequence with 'Because'; A lists the same design facts without a relation.

13.why: D states the full mechanism (seawater + volcanic ash -> tobermorite -> crack filling); C is an overreaching 'must be' and A, B are single comparisons.

14.why: B is the only option covering all three methods and their agreement; A, C, D are single figures.

15.why: C links two mechanisms to the outcome and glosses BDNF for an unfamiliar reader; B merely lists the same measures without a relation.

16.why: D states the whole causal chain in both directions (collapse and rebound); A, B, C are its separate links.

17.why: All four are single notes; D has the most internal structure (practice, how, effect) but this item reads like chance to me.

18.why: Two caveat options exist (C, D); D bundles two scope limits into one hedged statement, C only one, so I take D by the integration rule.

19.why: A concedes the fluctuation and still states the long-term direction with both endpoints; D takes the concession as the conclusion and reads as the trap.

20.why: A generalizes from the 11-of-12 and three-ocean counts to a claim about vent ecosystems; B, C, D are single notes including the exception.

21.why: A is the only option correcting the correlation into a non-causal reading; D overstates consistency and C is the bare result.

22.why: A carries the full causal chain (ash weathers -> releases minerals -> crops need them -> fertile); C lists two notes with no relation.

23.why: Only D sets the two retreat figures against each other with the multiple stated; A, B, C carry one measurement each.

24.why: B is the only option naming the common cause of all three changes; A, C, D pair the effects without the driver.
